newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former Japan bank chairman linked to scandal dies.
newsitem.headline: Former Japan bank chairman linked to scandal dies.

text.p: The former chairman of a Japanese bank embroiled in a racketeer scandal died in hospital on Sunday after earlier trying to hang himself, a hospital spokesman said.
Kuniji Miyazaki, 67, was questioned by authorities on Friday in relation to alleged payoffs to "sokaiya" racketeers.
"Mr Miyazaki has just died," a Tokyo hospital spokesman told Reuters on Sunday evening.
"He had remained unconscious since he was brought here this morning. He had been under intensive care," he said.
Miyazaki was chairman of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank during the time of payoffs to a racketeer who also has links to Nomura Securities in the current scandal.
He stepped down as a senior adviser to DKB in mid-June after admitting contacts with the racketeer. Miyazaki served as DKB president from 1988 to 1992 and as chairman from 1992 to April 1996.
